expectedMisconceptions: Children often assume more or thicker material automatically means a stronger bridge, missing that shape (folding, arching) usually matters more than quantity of material.

A first design that survives the test can get treated as 'finished' — worth encouraging at least one genuine refinement attempt even if the first try works, so the reflection on what changed has something real to say.
stretchQuestions: Could you make a bridge that holds even more weight using the exact same materials, just arranged differently?
What's the trade-off between building a stronger bridge and building a lighter one?
estimatedSupervision: Moderate — adult supervision recommended during the load-testing experiment (see `generated/resources/experiments.json`, Mission 7 entry); gathering craft materials (card, straws, tape) beforehand helps the session flow.
